en: Itivuttaka 28 Dukanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the monks approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him: “Friend Ānanda, this was said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the meaning and the phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is utterly perfect and pure. Now, friend Ānanda, what is that Dhamma that was spoken of by the Blessed One? “Friends, this is that Dhamma that was spoken of by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a destroyer of crops and the person who is a destroyer of seed. And how, monks, is one a person who is a destroyer of crops? Here, monks, a certain person destroys the crops of others, whether they have been sown or not yet sown, whether they have sprouted or not yet sprouted. This, monks, is called a person who is a destroyer of crops. And how, monks, is one a person who is a destroyer of seed? Here, monks, a certain person destroys the seeds of others, whether they have been planted or not yet planted, whether they have sprouted or not yet sprouted. This, monks, is called a person who is a destroyer of seed. These, monks, are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. “Indeed, friend Ānanda, this is that Dhamma that was spoken of by the Blessed One. “Furthermore, friends, this is that Dhamma that was spoken of by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a destroyer of crops and the person who is a destroyer of seed. And how, monks, is one a person who is a destroyer of crops?

The Discourse on Dwelling in Suffering (…) This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:

“Bhikkhus, possessing two qualities, a bhikkhu dwells in suffering in this very life—with vexation, distress, and fever. What two? (1) He does not guard the doors of his sense faculties, and (2) he is immoderate in eating. (…) “Bhikkhus, possessing these two qualities, a bhikkhu dwells in suffering in this very life—with vexation, distress, and fever. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. This is what I heard. (…)* *The full sutta includes further details regarding the guarding of the sense doors and moderation in eating, as well as their opposites.*
With the breakup of the body, after death, a miserable destination is to be expected.
By which two?
By not guarding the doors of the sense faculties and by lack of moderation in eating.
“Monks, a monk who possesses these two qualities dwells in suffering in this very life— with vexation, distress, and fever—
and after the breakup of the body, after death, a bad destination is to be expected.
Thus the Blessed One spoke.
In this regard, it is said:
“The eye, the ear, and the nose,
the tongue, the body, and likewise the mind;”
For that monk whose doors are unguarded and who lacks moderation in food, [the mind does not become concentrated].
One who is unrestrained in the sense faculties encounters bodily suffering and mental suffering— suffering indeed he attains.
With a body burning and a mind burning,
whether by day or by night,
“Such a person dwells in suffering.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The first [sutta].
